task.instruction: Prioritize a fix for a refill-return product whose customers complete requests but wait unpredictably for collection.
task.deliverable: A first-priority intervention, stable service promise, and supporting evidence.

evidence.content: Changing label copy needs one design day; changing batching rules needs three teams and can reduce the long tail by an estimated two days.

A synthetic return-policy register states that every already-issued return window remains honored while pickup labels or batching rules change; those operational changes cannot shorten a customer commitment.
A synthetic trace of 90 returns finds 62 delayed at the pickup-label screen and 21 delayed later by route batching.

A.content: Prefer a bounded intervention at the immediate decision point when wider changes are not required by the evidence.

B.content: Prefer an intervention that accounts for connected incentives and downstream effects when the evidence shows they matter.

irrelevant.content: Keep the artifact title concise enough to fit on one line.

decisions.prompt: What intervention scope should receive first priority?
regionOptions: repair the pickup-label decision point first
coordinate label, batching, and capacity changes as one system

T0: repair the pickup-label decision point first
coordinate label, batching, and capacity changes as one system
T1-A: repair the pickup-label decision point first
T1-B: coordinate label, batching, and capacity changes as one system

regionOptions: cancel existing windows while routing is redesigned

nonGoal: Do not revoke collection windows already shown to customers.
